newsitem.title: CANADA: EU-U.S. deal on Cuba must apply to all - Canada.
newsitem.headline: EU-U.S. deal on Cuba must apply to all - Canada.

text.p: A deal between the European Union and the United States to settle their trade dispute over Washington's anti-Cuba legislation must also apply to Canada and other countries, Canada's trade minister said on Friday.
"We will insist that it apply to Canada or to any other country, and I think the way the (anti-Cuba) law is written, it would have to anyway," Trade Minister Art Eggleton told reporters.
"The Helms-Burton (law) will not provide for discriminatory procedure against some countries and not others," he said.
The European Commission said on Friday that it struck a deal with the United States over the controversial Helms-Burton law that punishes foreign firms for doing business with Cuba.

The United States and Canada have been at odds over the measure. Executives of Canadian miner Sherritt International Corp. have been banned from entering the United States under the law because of the company's operations in the Communist-ruled island.
The EU and the United States reached an agreement just days before the EU presented its complaint at the WTO.
EU Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan said in a statement that the deal would "chart a path toward a longer-term solution through amendment to the Helms-Burton Act."

Earlier this week, Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien discussed the Cuba dispute with U.S. President Bill Clinton on a visit to Washington. The two leaders agreed to disagree on the best way to encourage democracy in Cuba.

While Canada maintains that that its commercial and diplomatic ties to Cuba will encourage the Castro regime to improve democracy and human rights, the United States argues that its embargo of Cuba is the best approach.
